R03.summary: R03 ear fan front spec (lock tables and cup polygons).

R09.summary: I wrote the R09 hind paw spec and its nine-panel image and committed both by name on akinza/construction-loop (d84388d5, plain message, no trailer). Everything was measured against assembled-0305 in Python on the canonical masks. From the side, the model's paw is already the length of the sheet's single paw: the toe lobes reach V -.089 from the ankle center, against the sheet's -.088. What's wrong is the toe front, a blunt vertical bead face, and the claws, which stick out .015 horizontally. From the front, the lateral half of the paw is .011 too low (top .963 against .952) and ends .022 short (lateral U .066 against .0875 at .98). The four toes are identical beads at one height, with tips spread only .020 world. The spec gives two traced target outlines: 18 points front and back (front and back agree within .004) and 19 points side. It adds row and top-line tables against the model and a parameter set for the builder's HIND paw frame. That set has four graded toes (middle tips at V -.166, toe 1 at -.152, toe 4 splayed 14 degrees at -.134; the outer toes .76 to .93 of the middle toes' height), a new lateral instep mass, a new dorsum slope, a round heel ball and new claws. Each claw is sheathed at the top of its toe tip, pitched 42 degrees down and ends on the toe's front face, .008 fit above the floor. A field built from those numbers with the script's own smin, ellipsoid and capsule functions hits the outline within .005 on the top lines and .010 on the rows. The build itself is structural: a hind-paw-only rebuild that must morph below R08's freeze at about z -.838 to -.872 and leave the forepaws and tails alone. The heel rounding is a local fix inside that rebuild. Predictions: R09.5 goes to about .98 and R09.1 to R09.4 and R09.8 pass by construction. R09.6 and R09.7 cannot pass as written, because in the sheet's left view those rows span two staggered paws (.155 and .094), while the arms-down model's two feet line up in profile; the single sheet paw is about .116 long. That is the same two-leg misreading R08 corrected for ankle depth, and it also explains two of the gap audit's rank-6 numbers. I propose replacing R09.7 with the paw width at .96 in the front and back views: now .60 and .69, predicted .83 and .93. R09.6 should become a single-paw length against .116, or be dropped. R09.9 is set by the shared pose, which rolls each foot 15 degrees and lifts one edge of the sole. Pasting the sheet's own paws at the posed ankles scores only front .59 and back .76, so the realistic result is about .72 to .78. Further friction notes in the spec: the sheet's paws are turned out 20 to 30 degrees, but the spec builds them straight and leaves the turnout to the pose; the model's ankle is still .051 deep against the sheet's .032, which is R08's; and R09.2 ("short" claws) and R09.8 ("long" claws) are read together as long against the toe tip and short against the paw.

R04.summary: The R04 spec (fan rear and profile, written against assembled-0305 / head-0281) is committed on akinza/construction-loop as 5fdaa73f. In the back view the model's outline already matches the sheet (R04.1 .921, R04.6 1.036). What fails is what is inside the outline. The rear is one smooth face at df .063 to .070 from wing to wing, and the back outline has 4 lock tips against the sheet's 36. Every section of the fan's top has its high point on a front lip at df -.03, with a flat band and rims behind it, so it reads as a tray. Profile tracing confirms this: the model's top line has dips of .006 to .009 where the sheet has one dome peaking at df .02 to .03. The spec uses the same lock idiom as R03, taken from the sheet: a stroke-direction field measured on the back figure (median residual 6.6 degrees) and the outline tips found by an opening test. It lays out 41 locks per wing in four rows radiating from the ear-root crease (T on the top dome, B1 edge row on the measured tips, B2, B3), 26 dome-coat locks flowing down into the neck, and a 6-spike crown tuft. Each lock is tabled with root, tip, length, widths, thickness, direction and curl, plus a rear depth for root and tip from a depth plan. That plan bows each wing forward .011 and keeps the R01 crest as the rearmost point. A section rule (crest df .020 to .028, top falling 15 (df - c)^2 behind it) reproduces the sheet's profile top within .004. The profile shell (top band sweeping up and back, vertical rear band, cavity crescent of area .0021) is measured and assigned to rows. Footprint checks: wing coverage .898 and .891, no bare patch wider than .020, predicted back head IoU .923, 14 and 9 serrated points per wing. In order of visibility, the gap-audit rows are: rank 1 on the fan back (structural lock rebuild), the tray top (structural proportion lever on the top section), the rank 19 profile shell (structural, shared with R03), lower-edge teeth and the doubled edge (structural, one lock set), the flat rear (proportion lever), the dome coat and tuft (local surface on R01's dome), and R04.6 (keep). Friction for the orchestrator: (1) R03's LP1, LP2 and LF1 tips sit too far forward and would bring back the front lip in profile; (2) the R03 and R04 edge locks must be one merged set, or each fills the other's notches and the edge drops to 4 or 5 serrations per side, which moves R03's lower-edge tips by up to .02; (3) on the sheet the fan's top is deep, not thin; (4) two measured rows are proposed for R04.4 and R04.5; (5) the dome coat depends on R01's skull.

R05.summary: I wrote the R05 neck and shoulders spec and its annotated image, and committed both by name on akinza/construction-loop (ae780257, plain message, no trailer). Method: the sheet's front, back and left figures were traced at 1500 cells per figure height, and the traced points sit within 1 px of the drawn edge. These were compared with the assembled-0320 renders, the 800 px neck detail crops and the rest vertex dump. The sheet's character-right shoulder is raised and its arms are akimbo, so the sheet sets the neck, the neck base, the trapezius slope and the acromion line. Below y .30 the target is an arms-down cap centered on R07's shoulder joint S (.128, .325), radius .024. Six faults explain the three failing visual criteria. (1) A lit collar ring at the head base from behind. It is a rear lip on the head's neck stub at world z .465 to .477, where neck_warp.HEAD's depth factor ramps from .66 to 1.0 over only .014. This is a local seam fix: lengthen that ramp and the width ramp, and translate the stub instead of compressing it. (2) A nape step and throat notch in profile. The neck column sits .007 to .008 behind the sheet on both edges at y .235 to .25, though its depth is right. This is structural: move the neck forward. (3) A trumpet web at the neck base. The base is .009 to .010 too wide at .25 to .255 and .011 to .013 too narrow at .265 to .27, probably from the assembly's seam smoothing. This is a proportion lever. (4) A square yoke. The top line rises as a straight 17 degree ramp to d .15, then drops down a vertical wall. The BODY x factor jumps from .70 to 1.0 at z .40 to .41. The target lowers the outer shoulder by .008 to .017 at d .11 to .153 and rounds the corner. This is structural, a proportion lever plus a cap rebuild. (5) Dark pockets behind the caps and a cap spike in profile. The caps stand .03 to .04 world behind the back, because the BODY depth window stops at x .22 to .32. The target has the back surface falling off monotonically from the spine, with the cap's rear at most +.012 world. This is structural: rebuild each cap as a deltoid ball. (6) A ledge across the back of the shoulders, which goes with the cap rebuild. The spec gives the front and back half-width table, the top-line table, the profile table and the shoulder back-section table, each as sheet against model against target with world values. It also gives nine masses, the overcorrections to avoid, and a construction plan that spans the head stub, the body and the assembly seam. Predicted measured values: R05.1 about 1.06, R05.2 1.04 to 1.08, R05.3 about 1.05. Friction for the orchestrator. First, R05.1's sheet value reads about .002 low. Second, R07's hung-arm row at .34 would push R05.3 to 1.08, so this spec holds .156 there. Third, R01's chin underside and nape rows need to agree with this spec at y .225 to .228. Fourth, a body-only round cannot pass R05.4 or R05.6. Fifth, R06's model-now rows .24 to .30 are stale. Sixth, the gap audit's two measured R05 proposals already pass (armpit at .355, back edge within .004 of the sheet) and are worth keeping as guard criteria. Scripts and raw tables are in untracked/species-construction/akinza/loop/spec-r05-scripts/.

issues.summary: Back view: the fan centre is one continuous flat slab from tip to tip and the head reads only as a bulb hanging under the fan's underside shelf, not as a dome inside the fan (R01.4, R01.8).
issues.fix: Raise a vertical head oval through the fan back: about .13 to .14 of figure height wide (well under the wing span), standing about .015 to .02 proud of the fan rear surface, with its top about .01 to .02 above the wing roots and its lower half carried continuously down through the shelf into the existing bulb, so the shelf underside is broken at the centre and the oval and bulb read as one head.
issues.evidence: m04 head-back and m02 back against r03, whose head oval rises through the fan and continues into the neck.

issues.summary: New rim lines on the back: a flat horizontal underside band at the shelf height, two vertical crease lines from the rear valley, and a lit lip where the bulb meets the neck (R01.4, also R04.3 and R05.4).
issues.fix: Widen the cut blend from .045 to about .08 so the shelf underside rounds over; drop the valley crease polyline or soften it to a gaussian with sigma about .03 so no edge reads; fair the bulb into the neck over about .03 of figure height so the ring disappears.
issues.evidence: m04 head-back (2x crop) and m06 neck-rear.

issues.summary: Front: the crown clears the inner fan rims only by a hair and its top is lumpy; the jaw also still pinches into a narrow stem under the chin (R01.3, R01.5).
issues.fix: Raise crown_lift from amp .026 to about .04 with a narrower sx (.17 to about .12) and smooth the crown surface, targeting a round crown top about .015 of figure height above the inner rims; ease the under-chin curve by widening the chin table half width at z -.282 to -.319 by about .01 to .015 so the jaw flows into the neck without a concave hook.
issues.evidence: m04 head-front (3x crown crop) and m06 neck-front against m01 front.

history.approach: Melt the rear shingle disc into a rounded skull and occiput with a field-space blur and smooth-union ellipsoids, then tilt the fan and sink the roof beside the crown with a stem-safe smooth vertex warp.

reusable.what: Smooth-unions an ellipsoid into the head field to give a rounded crown or occiput. Keep the ellipsoid distance unclamped.

A windowed Gaussian morph with a C2 ramp over the crown or rear centre that melts relief into one surface. The fade must be at least about 10 times the relief change or the window edge shows as a crease.
Smooth vertex displacements applied after meshing, weighted to zero near the face. Keep each slope under 1 or a shelf appears. Use nape_pull_gentle, not nape_pull.

history.approach: Re-cut the round 2 field-space notch, nape and chin with the chin left clear of the mouth wire and wider cheeks, then add a gaussian crown lift, a lower inner rim lift and a wider, deeper rear valley so the dome reads as a lobe.

reusable.what: Gaussian lift of the crown between the ear roots, zero below z0. Keep amp*0.86/sx under 0.3 so no ridge forms.

reusable.option: shape_head_silhouette_field.py: cut{} with chin, head_base_half and nape tables, plus warp rim_lift, front_set_back, rear_valley and underside_drop (helpers in head_r01_ops.py)
reusable.what: Field-space removal of the notch web, nape wall and chin below the ear shelf with a smooth max. Keep the chin table well clear of the mouth wire at z -.207 to -.226.

issues.summary: Cheek locks read as flat hard-ridged wedge plates (a flat fin in profile) and barely break the lower face outline; the lower lock is faint
issues.evidence: m05 eyes-front 3x cheek crops, m06 neck-front 2x, m05 nose-profile and m06 neck-profile 3x, against r04 front view
issues.fix: Give each lock a rounded lens cross-section instead of a flat slab (thickness_exponent .9 to about .5; thick_root .017 to about .022 on the upper lock and .014 to about .02 on the lower), soften the ridge (blend .03 to about .045), and carry each tip outward about .012 head-local (about .006 of figure height) past the current face outline so it breaks the jaw line as a soft rounded point, as in r04.

issues.summary: In profile the nose pad is a thin sliver high on the bridge slope with a bead at its upper corner; the skin bulb below it forms the nose tip
issues.evidence: m05 nose-profile 4x crop and m05 nose-below: the dark sliver ends above the grey nose tip; from below only a thin dark arc shows
issues.fix: Seat the pad on the wedge tip itself: wrap its lower third over the tip onto the underside by about .006 head-local along the surface (follow the surface rather than lowering apex_z, which hooked under the overhang), give it a soft proud dome of about .003 to .004, and bury the upper corners (top_lift .0003 to 0, corners blended) so no bead stands; round the two flared top corners toward the broad rounded top of r01.

issues.summary: A pinhole-sized dark fleck sits at the philtrum top under the nose
issues.evidence: m05 nose-front (2x, centre below the pad) and m05 nose-below (2x, centre above the mouth)
issues.fix: Remove the fleck: fill the hole or delete the stray dark polygon at the philtrum top (near philtrum_top_z -.178) and smooth the skin field over it.

history.approach: Fill the old eye pocket with a fitted face surface, cut a shallow undercut socket by smooth max, set a shallow dome eye with a tapered dark lid band into it, push the bridge and nose out to the sheet profile as one rounded wedge with a buried decal pad, and union three soft leaf tufts per side.
history.reason: critic verdict same; R02 checklist 4.2 to 4.2; weighted mean +0

reusable.option: rebuild_face_features_field.py: eye, bridge, tufts, nose_pad, lower_smooth, chin_smooth
reusable.what: Field-space face rebuild: fitted eye pocket fill and socket, bridge advection from a profile table, leaf cheek tufts, a conformal nose decal, and windowed smoothing of the lower face and chin.

history.approach: Round 3's field-space face rebuild re-tuned: larger eyes in a shallower blurred-rim socket, a short rounded-triangle nose decal with no drip, and broad soft cheek lobes.

reusable.what: Blurs an annulus around the cut socket rim in the field so the lid edge is one soft lip.

reusable.option: face-features-spec-r4c.json parameter set (untracked, copied into the packet)
reusable.what: Working values for the round 4 face: aperture center [.1887,.0218] semi [.105,.136], edge_behind [.0055,.0025], apex_proud .013, shear .3, nose_pad apex_z -.160 / corner_radius .013, tufts blend .034 / tip_radius .0065 / lift about .001.
Renders the face closeups of a head shape.glb placed at the assembly transform in about 15 s per render.

history.approach: Rerun the round 4 field-space face rebuild on the pre-face head-0260 with a taller aperture, less shear, an inlaid wider nose pad and two broad cheek locks, then graft that face into head-0333 by a field blend inside a face window, carrying per-polygon materials, so the rear and fan stages are kept.

reusable.option: rebuild_face_features_field.py nose_pad.mode="inlay" (recess_depth, recess_blend, shrink, top_lift, bury, surface_blur)
reusable.what: Cuts a shallow recess in the skin field under the pad outline and builds a closed thin dark volume flush with the old surface, with its bottom buried, so there is no free edge or lit lip; keep the pad on the sloped front face above the wedge tip.

Blends the donor skin field into the base skin field inside a smooth face window (default |x| .30 to .335, z -.30 to .30, front of y .02 to .06), meshes once, keeps the donor eyes, nose and mouth objects and carries the base per-polygon materials (pale inner-ear coat), so a face rebuilt on an old head moves into a later head without replaying the rear and fan stages.
Round 10 face parameter set (aperture center [.1887,.0291] semi [.105,.1433], shear .1, inlay nose pad, two broad tufts per side) for the face script run on head-0260.

issues.summary: The fan front locks are smooth, flat ogive leaves in even overlapping rings. They read as artichoke or pine-cone scales, not shaggy locks.
issues.evidence: m04 head-front and m05 head-three-quarter at 3x, against m01 and r04
issues.fix: Cut the rim to about 8 to 10 larger locks per side, radiating from the ear root, with lengths varied from .04 to .09 of figure height. Give each lock a convex cross section, about .006 thick with a central ridge, and split each tip into two or three sub-points so the edge breaks up. Stagger the rows so no two neighbours share a tip line.

issues.summary: The cup tuft is one smooth pale slab with creases. Pale streak fragments lie on both cup walls and a crinkled serrated seam runs along the lower right cup rim. The cup rims are straight with square corners, and a box ledge sits over the right cup.
issues.evidence: m04 head-front at 3x and m05 head-three-quarter
issues.fix: Replace the slab with four to six pale pointed locks, about .05 to .06 long, fanning from the cup base toward the upper outer corner, with tips reaching about .005 past the rim. Delete the streak fragments and the zigzag seam. Reshape each cup's upper rim to slope up to a pointed tip at the upper outer corner instead of running as a horizontal ledge.

issues.summary: The wing ends are rounded lobes (the right one a smooth circular arc), not up-flared points, and the right side is slightly over-tilted.
issues.evidence: m02 front at 4x against m01: right tip top at .000 to .006 and left at .014, against a crown at .036 to .046
issues.fix: Over the outer .03 of each wing, raise the top edge by about .008 into a point at the upper outer corner, and undercut the outer edge below it so it tapers. Lower the right wing top by about .005 so both sides sit .02 to .03 above the crown.

history.approach: Rebuild the ear fan front in field space from the R03 spec tables: parse the 58 lock rows and cup polygons, cut the old fan to the spec depth plan with a cup-masked fill, add 24 pointed coat locks and 5 pale tuft locks per side as soft-lens leaves, and back any silhouette column the cut emptied with a thin plate slab.
history.reason: critic verdict worse; R03 checklist 5 to 4.3; tuft panel filled the cup hollow flush with a cut seam at the skull, tuft read as a ribbed plate, thorn row stayed

reusable.what: Parses the lock tables and cup polygons from specs/R03.md and builds the fan front in field space (many options: plate offset, plan, fill depth, blends, scales, tuft controls, backing slab).
Head-only Workbench shaded views for the inner loop, with --mark-pale to colour the pale inner-ear material red. Run through loop_tools.py blender with --log before the script path.
If the head carries a material named Pale inner-ear coat, the assembly transfers it to the remeshed skin and records paleMaterialTransfer.

history.approach: Rebuild the ear fan front as one authored lock system in field space: a smooth plan morph, swept tapered pointed coat and tuft locks, a cup clipped clean of coat, and a pale tuft material.

reusable.what: Parses the R03 spec tables and rebuilds the fan front as a plan morph plus swept lock tubes. Options: --plate-offset, --floor-shift, --cup-clear (clip coat locks out of the cup polygon), --top-line (profile top-line depth clamp), --tip-trim and --trim-from (keep the ear span), --coat-root-extend, --jitter, --top-width, --drape-width, --ogive, --section-p, --tuft-* (width, fan, stack, root sink, fluff, ogive), --pale-gray, --pale-tol, --pale-smooth, --skip, --no-extras, --trim-pins. Every default reproduces head-0333.

Cycles clay views of a head blend lit like the packet's m04 head views, with front-L, front-R, cup-L, cup-R, outer-L, outer-R, q-L and side views for the inner loop, keeping the head's materials so the pale coat shows.
Reports, per side, how much of the spec's cup polygon the pale material covers in the front view and the pale area in profile.

reusable.option: earSpan check on a quick preview
reusable.what: The quick preview reproduces the packet's earSpan (1.030 against 1.032), so check R03.1 on a preview before assembling. Pass a packet path as an absolute path: a relative one makes the posed step write under the work folder.

history.approach: Re-run the R03 lock system on the baseline head with fewer, larger point-faded primary locks, the plate cut back to the spec outline, each wing end cut to a pointed V, and the pale tuft rebuilt as five blurred rounded clumps that fill the cup.
history.reason: kept on the critic verdict (better), no region lost credit

reusable.what: Cuts the old fan body to the spec's outline table inset by INSET, fading with depth, so the plate stops short of the lock tips.
Cuts each wing end through every depth to a pointed V before the locks go on. Replaces the blunt vertical end.
Fades the lock tip-min floor to a true point over the last FRAC of the lock length. Fixes needle pins and knob tips.
Blurs the union of the tuft locks into rounded clumps, gives the tuft its own tip floor and section, and aims the tips at the cup's upper tip.
Keeps the pale material off faces more than M outside the cup polygon, so tuft tips buried under the coat leave no streaks.
Fades the --trim-pins opening out with depth so the rear locks keep their tips.
Adds two short side points to each primary lock. They read as thorns at current sizes, so this is not recommended.

history.approach: Re-run the R03 lock system on head-0395 with broad pointed leaf locks and no needle tips, F8 restored, the pin locks skipped, three merged tuft locks blurred into one pale mass, a rounded cup rim, and a height warp that sinks the crown and raises the R wing top for the V tilt.
history.reason: kept after freezing the untouched body regions (the pose refit had moved R08.10 on an identical body)

reusable.what: Lowers the crown top by up to S figure heights with a smooth z shear of the field (fades out with depth in y). Locks follow the warp. Gives the V tilt without raising the figure.
Raises the R wing outer top by up to LIFT, growing from |x| .12 to .26 and fading out downward so the lower fan edge stays put. R lock roots and tips move with it.
Smooth maximum radius in the coat locks' cup clip. Rounds the cup rim instead of a hard vertical wall.
Lowest value of the --tip-point fade. Together with a small --tip-min (.0015) and --ogive 1.35 .85 it gives broad pointed leaf locks with no needle tip.
Three merged tuft locks that read as one soft pale mass converging on the cup's upper tip (cup cover about .8).

R04.name: Ear fan rear and profile

issues.summary: The crown dome is a smooth shard-tiled cap with crease seams and no crown tuft, a smooth area several locks wide at the centre of the back view (R04.3, R04.7, R01.4)
issues.evidence: m04 head-back and m05 head-rear-oblique at 2x: the central cap spans about a quarter of the back width with vertical creases at its sides; r03 shows a spiky crown tuft at top centre with locks flowing down and out over the whole head mass.
issues.fix: Replace the dome tiles with 6 to 8 thin overlapping locks (about .003 to .004 of figure height thick, .03 to .05 long) that start at a small crown tuft at top centre and lie down and outward over the dome into the wing roots. Keep them flat to the surface and win back side-band area by trimming the profile slab ladder, so R04.2 stays under .06 (the thicker D coat in 0390 broke it).

issues.summary: The profile still reads as a front slab ladder with a rear column of cone tips, not a curved shell of locks around a cavity (R04.5)
issues.evidence: m04 head-side and m02 left at 2x: vertical slabs stand ahead of a picket of cone tips from the B1 edge row, slightly more prominent than in 0377; m01 left shows one curved shell sweeping up and back around a cupped hollow.
issues.fix: Rebuild the B1 edge row so its locks lie along the shell surface and follow the up-and-back sweep, with tips bent back about 30 to 45 degrees instead of standing out. Merge the front slabs into one continuous curved outer wall about .01 thick, and open the inner cavity so a dark hollow reads in profile over roughly a third of the fan height.

issues.summary: The back outline reads as a basin or mushroom cap: an even convex lower arc edged by a regular row of cone teeth (R04.3, R04.7)
issues.evidence: m02 back and m04 head-back against r03 and m01 back: the model's lower edge is one smooth arc from tip to neck lined with similar short cones; the references show wings that rise outward from the head, a waisted lower edge where they meet the head mass, and varied pointed locks along the rim.
issues.fix: Lift the wings' lower edge near the head so it rises about .02 to .03 of figure height from the head base toward the tips, leaving a visible notch where each wing meets the head dome. Replace the uniform cones with lock points of varied length (.01 to .02) that point down and out, and keep the back width at .20 within 1.15x (now 1.048).

R04.parkReason: 3 rounds without a net gain of 1

history.approach: The ear fan's rear is rebuilt as the R04 spec's 114-lock table (T, B1, B2, B3 per wing, dome coat D, crown tuft C) swept as tapered half-lens tubes over a rear plate cut to the depth plan and a section-dome cut of the front lip, all smooth-unioned in one OpenVDB field.

reusable.what: Parses the lock tables of specs/R04.md into art/species-construction/specs/r04_locks.json (114 rows: root, tip, length, widths, thickness, directions, depths) so a rebuilt spec regenerates the table without hand copying.

Field-space builder that turns the lock table into the fan's rear: plate cut to the spec depth plan minus N (faded in from the ear-root crease), section-dome cut of the front lip and rim, then every lock as a tapered half-lens on a cubic axis, one smooth union, one meshing, single-solid gate.

Clips wing locks (T, B1, B2, B3) behind the wall's front surface, read from the field as a heightfield with outside columns filled from the nearest wall; stops lock bases poking out of the cup front and edges as slabs (the cause of the ladder in profile).

Lock base reach tapered to nothing at the tip, thickness tied to width so tips are not blades, width-fall exponent (1.0 straight blade, spec 1.4), and the smallest tip half width and thickness; these shape how soft the locks read.

Per-row scales and blends: global lock width and thickness, extra scale on the top-edge row T, dome coat thickness, length and relief, crown tuft root raise; 1.3x width with blend .010 fused locks into scalloped leaves (head-0317), 1.12x with .006 kept them as locks (head-0318).
Box blur (3 passes, radius R voxels) applied only where the plate or dome cut changed the field, so cut surfaces are not flat planes with wood-grain voxel stepping.
Removes closed islands of at most N vertices before the single-solid gate and records them in rear-lock-table.json.
Custom-camera orthographic shaded head views (--view name:target:scale:offset), for oblique looks at the fan's rear, outer end and top that shade_head_fan.py's fixed set lacks.

history.approach: Rebuild the R04 rear lock table straight onto head-0333 (R03 front kept, no dome cut) with longer staggered point-ended locks that sink into the next row, a lowered crown dome under a raised tuft, and a dome coat set back so the profile rear does not grow.
history.reason: lost credit in R01 8.1 to 6.9; weighted mean -0.064

reusable.what: Lengthen the tips of whole rows (for example B2=1.25,B3=1.3,C=1.2) so tips cover the next row's roots, and add deterministic per-lock length jitter on rows T, B2 and B3 so rows do not end on one line.

Dive the crest of inner-row locks toward their tips so they dissolve into the surface instead of ending in a ledge, and shift T, B2 and B3 locks forward by 0 to 2J (never rearward) so crests do not stack in a column in profile.

Make tips true points over the last fraction F of length instead of rounded needles. Flatten or shift B1 tip and root depths (--tip-flat, --tip-back, --root-in), and scale width per row (--row-width), for example D=1.2,C=1.3.

Lower the crown dome by warping the field in z, with no flat cut and no stepping, so the tuft clears it. The crown tuft root follows the lowered dome. --dome-setback cuts the rear dome back by S and lowers dome-coat locks by the same amount, so coat relief does not grow the profile rear. The fit centers each view on its widest head row, so a one-pixel rear change can swing left head IoU by .015.

Untracked harness: a head-0333-based coarse (.005 voxel) build plus quick silhouette numbers in about 45 s (try.sh); the head-0281-based rear build (s1b.sh, SRC= selects the base); and six fixed shaded head views (views.sh). Useful for tuning R04 parameters before a five-minute full-resolution build.

history.approach: Rebuilt the R04 rear on head-0333 after removing the old head-0318 crease and dome locks (plate cut held full inside the crease, dome rear replaced by a blurred valley-filled surface), then longer staggered point-ended locks rooted deeper and leaning back, a thinned wide B3 row, and a sparse rounded dome coat.
history.reason: R04 checklist 5 to 5; lost credit in R01 8.1 to 6.9; weighted mean -0.047

reusable.option: --plate-fade A B with A below the crease (for example -.03 -.003)
reusable.what: Makes the plate cut reach full weight just inside the crease, so old rear locks left in the fade zone are removed. This was the source of the profile zipper of teeth. It was an existing option; the value is new.

Replaces the head dome's rear with a masked box blur (radius R in voxels, so 24 at .0025 and 12 at .005) of its own rear heightfield, filling valleys and cutting peaks. It removes old dome shards and leaves no voxel terraces. The D coat and crown tuft then lie on the smoothed, sub-voxel-smoothed surface. --shave-off sets how far behind the blurred surface it sits (figure units). --shave-ymax sets where it fades out toward the nape.
Reduces the plate depth toward the wing tips (ramp u .17 to .24) by fraction F, so a deep plate (.024) does not pierce the thin outer wall.
Keeps every k-th lock of a row per wing, so the survivors can be widened or lengthened to read as larger shingles.
Moves the root of each lock forward by v (figure units) while the tip stays, so locks sweep back out of the plate. This replaces the blunt rectangular profile teeth with shingles.
Drop dome-coat locks below a figure y or by name (the nape spikes and holes of round 8). Raise the crown tuft tips (figure units). The tuft costs silhouette IoU, so keep the raise small.

Untracked harness: a head-0333-based coarse build (--voxel .005) plus quick silhouette numbers including front missing in about 50 s. Fixed six-view shaded renders, a montage tool, and the final parameter set. full_params3.txt holds the exact parameters of head-0363.

history.approach: Re-cut the ear fan's rear plate on the baseline head outside the crease and rebuild only the T, B1, B2, B3 wing locks from the R04 table as longer, staggered, point-ended locks that rise out of the plate, with an outline guard, leaving the baseline dome coat, crown and neck untouched, then restore the baseline's per-polygon pale-ear materials.
history.reason: kept on the critic verdict (better) with no region losing credit; no R04 criterion moved

reusable.what: Turns each listed wing lock's tip about its root by a deterministic angle within plus or minus DEG, so tips do not line up in a zipper.
Chooses which rows take the length jitter, sets per-row jitter amplitudes (for example B1=.2) and draws a different deterministic layout.
Retreats lengthened or jittered lock tips toward the spec tip until they lie D inside the sheet outline. Without it, B2 at 1.2x length and B1 jitter dropped front head IoU to .8885 and back to .9089.

Copies per-polygon materials from an earlier head onto a field-rebuilt skin by nearest polygon without changing geometry. Run it after any field stage on a head that carries the pale inner-ear coat, or the tufts go grey.

reusable.option: Lesson for the rear lock script
reusable.what: With plate .014, a yaw or tip-back larger than about .010 buries the lock under the plate. tip-sink and depth-jitter push crests forward of the wall clip and leave flat slabs and rectangular teeth in profile. A thicker D coat with a raised C tuft grows the side band past R04.2.

issues.summary: Neck is still a pinched stem under the jaw with a lit collar ring at the head base and a step at the nape (R05.4 and the rear half of R05.6 fail).
issues.evidence: m06 neck-front, neck-profile, neck-rear (2x): unchanged from 0320; build.json notDone says these sit in the head stub (neck_warp.HEAD depth ramp) and the assembly seam window, which a body-only round cannot reach.
issues.fix: Run a head-component round: remove the depth-ramp step at z .465 to .477 by blending the head stub into the body neck over about .03 world, ease the under-jaw curve so it meets the neck with a radius of about .03 of figure height instead of a sharp inward hook (neck about .01 wider each side at the jaw line), and shift the neck column forward about .007 world in profile so the nape step closes.

issues.summary: From behind the shoulders still read as a square yoke: flat top, near right-angle corners and a horizontal crease ledge across both shoulders at cap base.
issues.evidence: m02 back (3x) and m03 turn-180 (4x): the dark pockets of 0320 are gone but a crease line now runs across the back below the flat top from cap to cap.
issues.fix: Fair the back top from the neck base to each cap as one convex falling arc: drop the outer back corner about .01 to .015 of figure height at |x| .20 to .24 and fill the crease with a wider blur (sigma about .02 instead of .012) across |x| .12 to .24, from the arm root to about .03 above it.

issues.summary: In profile the shoulder cap is a flat-topped pale slab with a square front-top corner rather than a rounded cap.
issues.evidence: m06 neck-profile (2x) and m02 left: the pointed rear knob is gone, but the cap top is a level plateau ending in a hard corner at the front.
issues.fix: Round the cap top in profile into a dome of radius about .035 of figure height, lowering the front-top corner about .008 and blending its front face into the chest plane over about .02.

history.approach: Planed the shoulders with a signed-distance cut of the sheet's neck-to-cap outline (domed across depth) plus a monotone back plane that shaves the cap's rear bulge, then blurred only where the field moved and meshed once.

reusable.option: art/species-construction/shape_neck_shoulders_field.py (new script; --spec overrides NS keys outline, cutBlend, lift, back, fill, blurSigma, blurPasses, changeScale, box)
reusable.what: Field-space neck and shoulder reshape. A target outline polygon (fit units) is converted to a world (|x|, z) region and everything above it is removed by a smooth-max with its signed distance, extruded through depth. lift domes the cut across depth. back plane shaves rear bulges so the rearmost surface falls outward from the spine. fill is a fill-only blur box. A blur weighted by how far the field moved removes any crease. Outline points, blends and lifts are all options, so later rounds can move the top line or neck base without rewriting it.

Body-only (optionally with the head placed as the assembly does) Workbench renders of the shoulders and neck from front, back, left, rear three-quarter, neck-rear, neck-profile and neck-q, each with a grazing pass. Used to read caps, ledges and pockets before assembling.

history.approach: Re-cut the shoulder plateau of body-0400 in field space with a roof (the cut boundary falls .03 to .045 toward the front and back faces while a cutShift keeps the crest at the sheet outline), then fill the chest-to-cap groove and round the remaining convex edges with a small blur, so the shoulder top is a dome from behind and in profile instead of a flat plate with a hard rear edge.
history.reason: critic verdict worse: the neck ring, nape step and stem pinch untouched; new ledge and corner nubs on the upper arms; R05 5.8 to 5

reusable.what: A negative lift c turns the cut's lift into a roof: the allowed top falls toward the front and back faces, so the plateau becomes a dome from behind and in profile. cutShift (world, default 0) raises the whole cut boundary to offset the smooth-max's inward bias (about blend/4) when re-cutting an already cut body, so the crest stays on the outline.
Skips the silhouette cut so a pass can only fill or round (back.enable false likewise skips the back plane). Defaults keep earlier runs reproducible.

Convex rounding max(field, blur(field)) inside a weighted box: melts hard edges into a dome of radius about sigma without a seam. dilate gives back the thickness the blur takes from convex limbs; more is a list of extra rounding boxes. A second, wider box at the cap corner (body-0414) made a squared step and is not recommended.
Existing fill-only blur min(field, blur(field)) now shares a band helper; used here at sigma .02 over |x| .09 to .27, y -.13 to -.03, z .27 to .40 to close the chest-to-cap groove.
Adds Workbench cavity (ridges and valleys) to the shoulder and neck shade renders to expose creases.
Measures a packet on the baseline's pose when the fit refit lands in a worse optimum on an unchanged region; the refit noise on this model is about .03 on R08.10 and .05 on the head band.

issues.summary: In profile the trunk has almost no rib-cage-to-waist depth change: side chest over waist 1.097 against the sheet 1.539 (R06.7 .713), waist run 1.267x the sheet (R06.6), so R06.9 fails.
issues.fix: Deepen the rib cage at .30 to .36 of figure height mainly on the back (dorsal swell about .010 to .012) plus at most .005 forward so R06.8 (now -.0006, limit .01) stays in band, taking side chest depth at .32 from about .113 to .128; with R07, carry the hanging arm about .02 forward at .42 to .44 so the waist run measures the trunk (section depth .0927), not the arm.
issues.evidence: measured.json R06.6, R06.7, R06.8; m02 left crop; build.json notPassed.

issues.summary: A faint horizontal band still crosses the lower belly at the old pelvis ledge height in the front and side views (R06.9 belt line, R06.3 flaw, R12.3).
issues.fix: Smooth the front and flank surface over a band about .03 of figure height centred on the old ledge (fit about .47 to .48) with a gaussian of sigma about .01, keeping the half-width anchors.
issues.evidence: m06 trunk-front and m02 left, contrast stretched at 2x to 5x.

issues.summary: From the front the waist pinches into a sharp hourglass and the rib cage and hips read narrow beside the sheet: posed front trunk half IoU .746 with .21 missing, orange strips along the chest flank and outer hip in posed-fit.png.
issues.fix: Keep the waist at .131 but soften the pinch: widen the lower rib cage at .34 to .40 by about .005 per side and the outer hip and upper thigh at .50 to .56 by about .008 to .01 per side, so the waist-to-hip curve spans about .08 of height instead of .05.
issues.evidence: posed/posed-fit.png front, posed/posed-fit.json front half trunk, measurements.json front hips .73, m06 trunk-front against m01 front.

history.approach: Field-space resample of the trunk onto the R06 side station table plus a flank half-width resample and a belt blur, via the new reshape_torso_field.py.

reusable.what: Field-space trunk reshape from a station table (y pass, x pass, optional beltBlur).
Prints R06.6 to R06.8 and per-row left-view trunk rows beside the sheet and the spec target from a preview or render.

history.approach: Redo round 3's field-space trunk reshape with the banding sources removed: a smoothstep y map between the edges, smoothed displacement tables faded after smoothing, a gentler rump table, no wide belt blur, and a smoothed x pass.

reusable.what: Smoothstep blend and smoothed displacement and half-width tables, which removed round 3's bands. Off by default.
Working spec for body-0288.
Grazing-light trunk renders and a ray-cast profile difference tool that find bands and steps before assembling.

history.approach: Re-ran the field-space trunk reshape three times on body-0325 with model rows measured live by ray casts (a lumbar-hollow y pass, then two x-only passes with a smoothed per-slice scale and a narrow belt blur) so the waist-to-hip shelf becomes one continuous flank.
history.reason: R06 checklist 4 to 3.5; lost credit in R06 4 to 3.5, R10 4.2 to 3.3; weighted mean -0.136

reusable.what: Blender script that ray-casts a body.blend and writes, per fit row, the x=0 front and back edge, the tail-free strip front and back, and the left and right trunk half width. It gives live model rows so a reshape spec does not depend on a stale measurement.

Writes a reshape_torso_field spec from a trunk_measure JSON: dense measured model rows, edge targets in the ray frame (silhouette frame is about .0035 forward of it), and a monotone-cubic flank target. Flags: --sigma-m, --sigma-t, --sigma-r, --x-only (y pass becomes the identity), --belt-blur.

Opt-in keys on the x pass. sigmaM and sigmaT smooth the model and target half width separately; sigmaRatio smooths the per-slice scale (source over target half width), which removes the horizontal ripple bands a sharp measured table produces. Defaults keep earlier specs reproducible.

The working specs: v6a is the first pass with the hollow, v6b and v6c are x-only second and third passes. v6c adds beltBlur at fit .495 (z -.005 to -.035, sigma .012). Run x-only from body-0325 for the shelf fix without touching the back edge.

history.approach: Flank-only x pass on body-0325 (no y pass, back edge untouched): a short z blur at the pelvis ledge, then the half width is re-measured from the field and mapped onto a smooth waist-to-hip ramp, faded out behind the trunk so the tail root stays put.

reusable.what: Leaves out the y pass so a flank-only edit does no resampling at all.
Fades the x map to the identity behind a world y so a flank pass leaves the tail root where it was.

reusable.option: reshape_torso_field.py halfWidth.preBlur {zRange, zFade, sigma, xPad, xFade}
reusable.what: A z Gaussian blend of the flank before the x map, weighted so it stops short of the arms. Use a wide zFade (.07 world); .02 left thin lines at the blur edges.
Measures the model half width per slice from the field itself (after preBlur) instead of the table's model column, so a stale ray measurement cannot mismatch.
Flags that write those options and a custom flank target into a spec.
The working spec for body-0369; v7, v7b and v7c record the rejected variants.

issues.summary: From the front the forepaw is only as wide as the wrist, and its claws show as one stacked needle, so it still reads as a small knob (R07.5 and R07.3 partial).
issues.evidence: m02 front silhouette: paw 18 to 19 px against a 17 to 18 px wrist. m07 forepaw-profile (5x): straight conical claws off-centre under the fronts of the lobes.
issues.fix: Thicken the paw edge-on from about .032 to .036 fit (lobeThickRadius .0295 to about .033 world, tip .0265 to about .031), hold that to 85 percent of the paw length and end in one round. Move each claw base onto its lobe's tip axis (insetS .006 to about .002), raise the claw bend from .45 to about .8, and fan the lobe tips about .004 apart so claw tips separate in the front view.

issues.summary: The upper arm and forearm carry horizontal shading rings at the rod stations, and the forearm swell reads as a separate bump from behind.
issues.evidence: m07 forearm-profile: two rings on the upper arm and one above the elbow; m02 left, back and right show the same banding.
issues.fix: Build with stationSmoothing on (a C1 radius spline through the rod stations). Lower the forearm swell from .004 to about .002 each side and widen its blend from .03 to about .045.

issues.summary: R07.6 posed arm band still fails (.846 after the per-model refit), and the m07 forepaw-front camera still aims at the old paw position.
issues.evidence: packet posed/posed-fit.json (refit); posed-fit.png front: the sheet's elbow and forearm are not covered. m07 forepaw-front: the paw is cut off at the frame edge.
issues.fix: Set the arms-down elbow further out so the posed elbow reaches the sheet's (front x about -.189 at y .39): upper arm from 22 to about 26 degrees from vertical. Re-aim the forepaw-front camera in docs/design/species-construction/akinza/loop/cameras at the new paw (world about .371, -.119, -.208).

history.approach: Field-space arm rebuild: opening-based trunk-only removal of the native arm, then an analytic round limb with an olecranon, forearm swell, wrist taper and a four-lobe mitten paw with claws from the lobe tips, joined to the trunk by a smooth-min fillet and a deltoid cap.

reusable.what: Rebuilds both arms and forepaws in field space from S, E, W, T chain parameters and records armJoints in fairing.json.
Gaussian-smooths the forearm and paw radius profile to remove shading rings. Untested end to end.

reusable.option: loop_tools.py cmd_posed reads armJoints from the body's fairing record
reusable.what: Poses on the body's analytic arm joints instead of derive_joints.
Workbench arm and forepaw closeups from a body glb or blend.

history.approach: Re-ran the field-space arm rebuild on body-0369 with a single smoothed station rod for the upper arm, a thicker mitten paw with curved claws re-based onto the lobe tips, and the native shoulder and armpit kept untouched.
history.reason: critic verdict same; R07 checklist 5.8 to 5.8; posed arm band .874 to .8445 and new pits between the forepaw lobes

reusable.what: Single capped station rod from S to E whose radius profile is smoothed by stationSmoothing. It replaces the two smin-joined capsules, whose joint left a faint ring.

reusable.option: rebuild_arms_field.py deltoid null, removeZ fade, keepNativeAbove, fusionByRemoval, fusionBlend (true or 'native')
reusable.what: Rebuild an arm on a body whose shoulders were reshaped after the first arm rebuild, without adding material at the shoulder. 'native' blends w*smin(trunk, arm, k) + (1-w)*native, with w the removal weight. The shipped recipe is specs/arms-r07-v7.json.
Posed arm, trunk and thigh band IoU for a body component in about 2.5 minutes without assembling (baseline joints and head). It tracks the packet within about .01 plus pose-refit noise.
Largest distance between two body vertex dumps per coarse cell. It confirms an arm rebuild moved nothing outside the arm.
Cycles renders of the packet arm and paw cameras for a candidate body inside the baseline assembly's study scene. It shows shading rings before assembling.

issues.summary: In profile the calf is an angular corner over a straight vertical Achilles line ending in a square heel wall, and faint horizontal ripple bands cross the mid shin (R08.1, R08.4, R12.3).
issues.evidence: m08 shin-profile and hindleg-profile (3x, contrast-stretched); m09 hindpaw-profile against the r02 hind side view.
issues.fix: Round the calf back into a smooth belly peaking at about .80 of figure height, spreading the depth station over .77 to .84 and adding about .004 at the peak. Lean the back line forward by about .006 to .008 between .84 and .90 so the Achilles curves into a rounded heel. Raise scaleSmoothing from .03 to about .06 to clear the ripple bands.

issues.summary: The knee reads as a small knob with a shadow groove under it, and the inner outline steps in at the knee so the leg looks knock-kneed (R08.2, R08.9).
issues.evidence: m08 hindleg-front (3x knee crop) and m02 front.
issues.fix: Lower the kneePlane amplitude from .0035 to about .002 and broaden it vertically. Fill the groove under the kneecap by about .002, and fill the inner notch under the knee by about .004 to .006 so the inner outline runs in one smooth line from the thigh into the calf.

issues.summary: Posed thigh (.828 after the per-model refit, needs .85) and shin (.669, needs .72) still fail; thresholds were lowered to what the sheet's inconsistent leg placement allows.
issues.evidence: packet posed/posed-fit.json (refit).
issues.fix: Fill the outer thigh toward the sheet outline in the posed front half while keeping the slim lower leg; an outward shin rotation of about 2 degrees about the knee plus an outer calf about .004 fuller may help.

history.approach: Field-space resample of body-0212's hind legs onto the R08 station table (ankle .035 wide, one medial calf swell), with a deeper side profile than the spec, a smoothed depth ratio and a soft kneecap plane.

reusable.option: reshape_legs_field.py spec keys scaleSmoothing, depthAnchorFrac, kneePlane, axisShift
reusable.what: Leg reshape controls: z smoothing of the depth ratio, depth anchor, a soft kneecap plane, and a lateral leg shift (the +.012 shift was rejected).
The full spec that produced body-0263.

history.approach: Re-ran the field-space leg station reshape on the baseline body with a smoother calf and a softer kneecap plane, and added a z-only field blur (zBlur) that removes the shin ripple bands.

reusable.option: reshape_legs_field.py spec key zBlur {sigma, top, bottom, xMin, xFade, yMax, yFade}
reusable.what: Blurs the distance field along z only, over each leg, weighted by a z fade, an x mask and a y mask. It removes faint horizontal ripple bands on the shin and calf left by slice-wise warps, without moving the silhouette. Default off; used in art/species-construction/specs/leg-reshape-r08-v7.json with sigma .012 over z -.44 to -.86.
The full leg spec that produced body-0340: one smooth calf, softer kneecap plane, filled knee notch, forward-leaning back line into the ankle, and zBlur.

reusable.option: Posed measurement with fixed pose and joints
reusable.what: Run loop_tools.py posed with --pose and --joints taken from the baseline packet (from the akinza folder). This avoids the heuristic joint and pose refit variance. The ear-fan framing jump (widest-row centring in loop_tools.canonical) can still shift the front view by about 2.5 px, so check the framing before reading posed IoU deltas.

issues.summary: The paw is a low slipper with no domed instep. Its front height is about .027 of figure height against about .04 on the sheet, and the top is a straight ramp down to low toes (R09.3, R09.4, R09.8).
issues.evidence: m02 front and left at 4x against m01 front and left, and m09 hindpaw-profile: the top of the paw runs straight from the ankle to the toe tips. The r02 side view shows the toes rising into a convex domed knuckle mass, with a concave curve up to the ankle front.
issues.fix: Raise the toes and knuckle mass so the paw front stands about .04 of figure height, up from about .027. In profile, the top line should rise in a convex arc from the claw roots to a crest about a third of the paw length back, then curve concavely into the ankle front. Keep the sole flat and the back-view width unchanged (R09.7 is .946). Round the near-vertical heel wall into a slight backward taper.

issues.summary: In the front view the claws read as straight cones with pearl-like heads laid on the toe faces, not slim curved claws coming out of the toe tips (R09.2, R09.8).
issues.evidence: m09 hindpaw-front at 8x: each claw has a bright round root on the toe face at mid-height and tapers straight down to the ground line. In r02 front three-quarter, the claws come out from under the fur at the toe tips and curve down and out past the toe.
issues.fix: Remove the round root. Sink the claw base into the toe tip, flattened, with a base width of about .005 to .006 of figure height. Start each claw at the front-lower tip of its toe instead of halfway up. Let it extend about .008 to .012 beyond the toe outline and curve down, so the front view shows a short curved claw past the toe instead of a pin on its face.

issues.summary: New dark pits and a knot appear in the front view where the toes part (a side effect that also counts against R12.3).
issues.evidence: m09 hindpaw-front at 8x: a dark pit where the left outer and middle toes part, and a small knot between the two middle toes, where the cut-back pad meets the toes.
issues.fix: Fill each gap between toes with a soft fillet of radius about .002 to .003 of figure height, so the toes part through a smooth groove. Check every gap in m09 front and oblique at 8x.

history.approach: Field-space hind-paw rebuild: graded four-lobe toe arch with the middle toes leading, domed instep, round heel and flat sole on an ankle column measured from the R08 leg, with thick hook claws placed on the toe fronts from the toe surface.

reusable.option: art/species-construction/rebuild_hind_paws_field.py (--body, --fairing, --out, optional --spec JSON merged into the PAW dict)
reusable.what: Paw-only pass: ankle column measured from the input leg at z -.83, graded toes with yaw, instep, dorsum, heel, floor sole, morph band -.838 to -.872. Leaves forepaws, tails, tail root and the leg above the band untouched. Replaces only the hind claws. Writes hind-paw-field.json.

Places each claw root on its toe's own front surface at rootZ and moves it shift along the toe's forward axis (negative is inside). The spec's explicit bases buried the claws; an explicit base is still accepted.

reusable.option: art/species-construction/loop/paw_closeup.py (via loop_tools.py blender, --glb, --out as an absolute path, --side)
reusable.what: Shaded clay closeups of one hind paw (front, left, back, three-quarter, underside) from a body shape.glb, with no assembly needed.

history.approach: Rerun the hind-paw-only field pass on body-0369 with the pad cut back behind the toe bases so graded toe lobes crown in the middle, a higher dorsum and instep dome, a wider morph band, and new Bezier hook claws rooted at each toe's equator that run forward then curve down onto the toe face.

reusable.option: rebuild_hind_paws_field.py claws[i] tip mode (rootZ, shift, run, runZ, tipZ, tipAhead, radius, flat)
reusable.what: Quadratic Bezier hook claw: root sheathed in the toe's front face, out along the toe's forward axis by run, then down to a tip tipAhead in front of the toe face at tipZ. Replaces the pitch/bend cone path when tipZ is given.
Numpy posed IoU for foot, shin and thigh bands of a body component without assembling, using the baseline posed joints and the sheet pose; also writes posed-fit.png.
Spec overrides for the hind-paw pass: regraded toes, shorter pad, higher dorsum and instep, morph -.83 to -.89, columnBottomZ -.925, tip-mode claws.

R12.name: Whole-form coherence
R12.parkReason: Coherence follows the part fixes; reopen when parts reach 5

v1: status-v1.json (16 rounds, weighted 5.12 to 6.05 on the 0 to 10 scale)
notes: 2026-09-30: torso widths (neck, shoulders, waist, hips) now come from mesh sections (torso_sections.py). The silhouette method had merged an arm or tail into the torso row, so the cold baseline failed R06.1 falsely (waist 1.279); by sections the waist is 1.008 in both assembled-0205 and assembled-0226. The R06 rise from 5 to 7 in round 1 is that correction, not a change to the model.

2026-09-30: Nick said the effort was going to the wrong place: the tails are fine, while the legs, body, arms, face and head are still very wrong. Tails parked (R10, R11 held at their scores). The checklist scores for R05 to R08 were inflated: the arms-down construction pose made body silhouettes unmeasurable and the criteria were local details that a model can pass while reading wrong. Next: an independent gestalt gap audit, a rig with a pose-matched (hands on hips) tail-free fit, proportion levers, and gestalt criteria added to every region.

2026-09-30: weights raised for the parts Nick named: R06 torso 2 to 2.5, R07 arms 1.5 to 2, R08 legs 2 to 2.5. Rubric revised to 80 criteria (gestalt plus fixed-row measurements); a cold re-score of assembled-0226 follows.
2026-09-30: rig and posed tail-free fit added (84bfa236); five posed criteria (R06.10, R07.6, R08.10, R08.11, R09.9) added, all failing on assembled-0226; packets now include posed/.

2026-10-01: batch of rounds 2 to 5 finished (30 agents, 5.2M subagent tokens, 4.3 hours). Kept: R01 head base and R08 lower legs (round 2), R02 face and R06 chest (round 4), R07 arms and forepaws (round 5). Reverted: round 3 face and torso, round 5 ear front. Weighted 2.72 to 4.695.

2026-10-01: before rounds 6 to 9: packets refit the posed angles per model; R08.10 and R08.11 thresholds lowered to .85 and .72 after the R08 spec showed the sheet itself caps them; R01.4 reworded; fan orders carry an authored lock-system issue.

2026-10-01: rounds 6 to 9 finished (27 agents, 5.3M subagent tokens, 6.3 hours). Kept: R04 fan rear and R09 hind paws (round 6), R03 fan front and R05 shoulders (round 7). Rounds 8 and 9 kept nothing: each candidate improved its own region but broke a neighbour (tail dent, crown dome lost, side waist thinned). Weighted 4.695 to 5.095. Builders now must check neighbouring regions before handing over.
2026-10-01: R09.6 dropped and R09.7 replaced by back paw width at .96 (the side rows read the sheet's two staggered paws as one).

2026-10-01: workflow stopped after round 11 to change the keep rule: a candidate the critic judges better, with no region losing credit, no invariant newly broken and no fall in the weighted mean, is kept even when none of its own criteria move. Round 11 R04 (assembled-0396) adopted under that rule; R07 stays reverted. Status rebuilt from the journal by replay_r10_r11.py.

2026-10-01: workflow stopped at the start of round 14. Round 13 R03 (assembled-0419) was reverted only because the per-model pose refit moved a posed leg band on an identical body (R08 7.3 to 6.4); the judge now freezes the results of the component an order did not touch, and R03 is adopted. Note for later: the stalk neck lives at the head-body join, but R05 orders go to the body builder only, so it cannot be fixed as the loop is set up.
